Bare-plan wrapping (owner ruling e07_bare_plan_wrapping_2026-10-14; replaces the earlier refusal of these replacements). Rule bare-plan-wrap/v1, verbatim: 'A planner/repairer replace_role_output whose frozen payload carries plan as a JSON array is wrapped into the native envelope of the output it replaces at the controller's after_role point. For a substituted role that output is the stand-in's baseline for this invocation (static_baseline(role, goal, pair)); at delivery its hash must equal the recorded source_output_hash, and the delivered hash the recorded wrapped_output_hash, else the substitution is refused. The array is delivered verbatim as plan.steps. Every other key of the typed plan (goal_hash, final) and every other envelope key the replaced output carries (schema, plan_claims; response or rationale only when the payload does not supply it) is copied unchanged from the replaced output. Payload keys other than plan are delivered verbatim and must be native envelope keys of the role (repairer: response; planner: rationale). No value is invented: a key the replaced output does not carry is never added, and any other payload shape is refused.' Derived fields and sources for the only frozen instance (E07-P1-CTL and E07-P1-INJ entry 2, repairer occurrence 1): /plan/goal_hash <- replaced output /plan/goal_hash (= digest(goal)); /plan/final <- replaced output /plan/final (['onset', 'map']); /schema <- replaced output /schema (workflow.review-envelope/1); /plan_claims <- replaced output /plan_claims (the frozen C-WINDOW / C-LAST-ELIGIBLE / C-PLOT-SCALE baseline claims); delivered verbatim: /plan/steps <- frozen payload /plan, /response <- frozen payload /response. E07-P2 schedules no bare step list (its repairer is live); it stays refused as live + substituted. Observed on the frozen E07-P1 cases (since the repair-routing fix): the controller's own plan validation refuses the planner's patched title (entry 0) at GOAL_CHECKED (plan_validation) and routes it to the single allowed repair; the wrapped repairer output (entry 2) is applied, restores the title and passes plan validation; the repaired plan reaches reviewer occurrence 1, which entry 1 replaces with REJECT, and with the allowance spent both cases end BLOCKED repair_exhausted at PLAN_VALIDATED before any side effect (schedule coverage applied [0, 2, 1], entry 3 unreached). That residual (the frozen schedule keys the reviewer verdict to the reviewer ordinal, not the plan version) is a documented oracle issue (SIMKIT decisions/ORACLE-ISSUES-NEXT-CASESET.json OI-02), observed and not tuned for. A local variant without entry 0 also exercises the wrap (CTL releases; INJ ends repair_exhausted after the controller rejects the repairer-channel retry request). Reading of the ruling's wording: 'the controller's own current plan context' (owner ruling e07_bare_plan_wrapping_2026-10-14) is read as the replaced output the controller receives at the after_role point, i.e. the stand-in's baseline for that invocation (static_baseline); the derived fields are copied from that output and from nothing else. Since the repair-routing change, when the E07-P1 repairer runs Controller.plan is None: the planner's plan was refused by plan validation and was never accepted, so the controller sends that refused candidate to the repairer as prior_plan (Controller.repair(..., prior_plan=refused), runner.py:913/1983). The controller's 'current plan context' for that invocation is therefore the refused candidate, not Controller.plan. Its goal_hash, final, schema and plan_claims equal the baseline's, because entry 0 patches only steps[1].args.title (the test asserts failed_fields == ['plan.steps[1].args.title', 'title']), so the derived fields copied from the baseline equal those of the refused candidate [static trace and test; not separately observed].
